player.seasonOutlook: Kessler has been a per-minute standout that is slowly building up his MPG. For his career, Kessler has averaged 13.4 points, 13.2 rebounds and 3.4 blocks per 36 minutes. Last season he played a career-high 30.0 MPG, but also a career-low 58 games. The end result had Kessler finish in the top-60 in fantasy points scoring average, but barely in the top-75 in total fantasy points. Kessler is only 24 years old and still improving, but he also has some difficulties playing against small-ball lineups and now has veteran pure-center Jusuf Nurkic as his backup as opposed to the departed John Collins, who also plays power forward. These factors could limit his minutes. Still, Kessler has top-50 upside this season.

Podziemski enters his third season as the frontrunner to be named the Warriors' starting shooting guard. He thrived post-All-Star break, averaging 15.5 PPG, 5.9 RPG and 3.7 APG while shooting 46.5% from the field and 43.8% from deep. His role is safe for now, with De'Anthony Melton expected to be eased back from injury and Buddy Hield likely the main competition for production. Podziemski offers steady scoring, elite shooting percentages and sneaky playmaking and rebounding. He is a great late-round fantasy target with room to grow.

The Trail Blazers traded leading scorer Anfernee Simons and released fifth-leading-scorer Deandre Ayton this offseason, replacing both with more defensive-minded players. This really opens up the opportunity for Avdija and Shaedon Sharpe to be the leading offensive engines in the starting lineup. Avdija is coming off a breakout campaign in which he set or tied career-best marks in all six fantasy hoops counting categories for the season. He showed flashes of dominance last season, including averaging almost 27 points with 11 rebounds in his last 13 games, giving him upside to have another breakout campaign in 2025-26.

White is coming off the best season of his career, establishing new career-highs in scoring, rebounds and 3-pointers per game as the third option on the Celtics. With Jayson Tatum out for the season and Jrue Holiday traded to Portland, White could have more responsibility for the Celtics this season. He will be relied upon to not only knock down open looks, but to also create more for himself and teammates. His scoring and assists could both see an uptick this season, moving him further into impact territory.

Antetokounmpo remains on the short list of best fantasy producers in the NBA, coming off back-to-back seasons averaging over 30 points, 11.5 rebounds and 6.5 assists per game. Those numbers came largely with Damian Lillard as his point guard, but in 14 games without Lillard, Giannis averaged slightly more points (31.1 PPG) and almost a full 1.5 more assists (7.9 APG). With Lillard gone this season and shooting big man Myles Turner in the fold as another finisher, Antetokounmpo has even higher upside this season with an outside shot at flirting with a triple-double.

Giddey finished last season with the best extended run of his career. Starting Feb. 20, he was a decimal-point away from averaging a 20-point triple-double over his last 19 games. The Bulls rewarded Giddey with a huge contract extension this offseason, and the plan seems to be to build around him as the main cog moving forward. If he continues this season like he finished last, he has top-20 fantasy hoops upside.

Poeltl played a career-high 29.6 MPG last season, which led to him setting new personal bests almost across the board. He finished decimal points shy of averaging a double-double, and for the first time averaged more than a steal and a block per game. Poeltl is still only 29 years old and at his peak, and he remains the only proven center on the Raptors' roster. He has played in just 107 of a possible 164 games in the last two seasons, but Poeltl was a top-55 players in fantasy scoring average last season and has top-50 upside this season if he stays healthy.

The Warriors are a team that fits both Butler's strengths and his weaknesses as a player, allowing him to be a second option that isn't relied upon as heavily in the regular season with the upside for him to dust off "Playoffs Jimmy" once the postseason arrives. For fantasy purposes, Regular-Season Jimmy on the Warriors is a good player, but one with capped upside. He's more likely to average in the upper-teens of points per game than the 20s he averaged with the Heat. He also seems likely to miss games as he manages injury to get through the season. Butler hasn't played more than 65 games since 2016-17, and with his likely absences added into the projections it drops Butler to a mid/late-mid-round pick in fantasy leagues.

Garland is coming off a season in which he set new career-highs with 75 games played, 2.8 3PG and 47.2 FG% even though he, like the rest of the Cavaliers' starting five, played a career-low in minutes (30.7 MPG) because the overall unit was so strong. But Garland suffered a toe injury late last season, had offseason surgery and is expected to still be out recovering early in this campaign. When he returns, he likely returns to a very similar role and production as last season. But before last season he had never played 70 games in an NBA campaign, and it appears he will miss that games threshold again this season.

The Cavaliers are in a tricky spot with Hunter. Max Strus' injury will likely push Hunter into the starting lineup, but he has historically been more efficient as a sixth man. He averaged 16.0 PPG and shot nearly 39% from deep when coming off the bench, compared to 14.4 PPG as a starter. Cleveland may try to manage rotations so Hunter can still lead the second unit, but early in the season, he'll likely play heavier minutes with Donovan Mitchell and Evan Mobley dominating touches. Expect solid volume early, but keep an eye on whether Hunter shifts back to the bench midseason. That is when his scoring efficiency and fantasy value typically spike.
